posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption:
A piece of paper, a crayon, and 30 minutes of sketching can make someone’s day. ✏️💛⁠
@sharuki.nags showed us how a simple drawing for the people of Kyoto turned into a small but meaningful moment of happiness.⁠
⁠
Sometimes, it really is the little things that make the biggest difference.

Madagascar is home to one of the world’s most unforgettable views: the Avenue of the Baobabs.⁠
⁠
Near Morondava, dozens of towering Grandidier’s baobabs line a dirt road in western Madagascar, creating one of the island’s most recognizable landscapes.⁠
⁠
The trees can reach around 30 meters tall, and the avenue is especially striking at sunset, when their huge silhouettes stand out against the sky.⁠
⁠
By: @graphicnode

This is your sign to face your fears and enjoy the ride. 🏔️⁠
Don’t let fear stop you from trying something new, chasing an adventure, or experiencing life to the fullest.⁠
⁠
Sometimes, the best memories start right where your comfort zone ends. 👀⁠
🎥: @tandembasemoab

Helsinki now has an island dedicated entirely to saunas.⁠
⁠
Saunasaari opened in June, just a short water-taxi ride from the city center. The island has traditional smoke saunas, Finnish wood-fired hot tubs, and views across the water toward Helsinki.⁠
⁠
And, as is tradition, you can cool off with a dip in the Baltic Sea after your sauna.⁠
⁠
It’s a pretty fitting addition to a city where sauna culture is part of everyday life.⁠
⁠
By: @woodward.creative

Statues in Glasgow always seem to be wearing a traffic cone. ⁠
The tradition dates back to the 1980s, when someone placed a traffic cone on the Duke of Wellington statue. The city kept removing it, but someone kept putting it back.⁠
⁠
Eventually, the cone became a symbol of Glasgow’s humor and its famously playful attitude. Today, it’s one of the city’s most recognizable quirks.⁠
So if you spot a statue with a traffic cone on its head, you know you’re in Scotland. 😂⁠
⁠
🎥: @ellistravelling

Zhongshuge Bookstore has several locations across China, but its Chengdu branch in Dujiangyan is one of the most famous. ⁠
⁠
This space turns reading into a visual experience shaped by light, height, and architecture.⁠
⁠
Towering bookshelves stretch across multiple levels, creating a strong sense of depth from every angle.⁠
⁠
Would you visit it?⁠
⁠
By: @kankankavee @jasonmengvisuals @irmabasheska @chintapha_2004

How fun is a battle where everyone is trying to be more polite? ⁠
In Japan, showing respect is a big part of everyday culture, sometimes it can even turn into a hilarious back-and-forth of who can bow first.⁠
⁠
Never back down from showing respect! 😂⁠
🎥: @worldofniki

Le Plongeoir sits on a rocky outcrop in Nice, France, with its dining room suspended above the sea. ⁠
⁠
The restaurant takes its name from the old diving board that once stood on the same spot, a landmark that has been part of Nice’s coastline for more than a century.⁠
⁠
Today, the historic structure has been transformed into one of the city’s most unusual restaurants, where every table comes with a view of the water below.⁠
⁠
Would you have dinner here?⁠
⁠
By: @leplongeoir

Baby bats getting their little treat of apple juice. 🦇🍎⁠
A beautiful moment captured by @maddyhny while feeding these adorable fruit bat babies in the wild.⁠
⁠
We don’t usually think of bats as cute… but these little ones might change your mind.

You can stay inside a giant serpent in Mexico.⁠
⁠
El Nido de Quetzalcóatl sits in the hills of Naucalpan, just outside Mexico City, and looks just like a fantasy movie setup.⁠
⁠
Designed by Mexican architect Javier Senosiain, the building takes its shape from Quetzalcóatl, the Aztec feathered serpent god. Its colorful, curved structure winds through gardens, trees, streams, and caves.⁠
⁠
Inside the serpent are 10 apartments, connected by curved corridors, bridges, and staircases. The design was

One of Ireland’s most famous traditions.⁠
Kissing the Blarney Stone is said to grant the “gift of eloquence,” but getting to it is an adventure of its own.⁠
⁠
Perched high within Blarney Castle, visitors must lean backwards over a drop to complete the centuries-old ritual.⁠
⁠
Not the easiest route to go through, but definitely one for the bucket list. ⁠
🎥: @raaachelfarmer

Photographed by @thomaspeschak, southern rockhopper penguins navigating the rocky cliffs and crashing waves of Marion Island—one of two Prince Edward Islands off the coast of South Africa. Named for their habit of hopping rather than waddling along rugged shorelines, they are characterized by the spiky black-and-yellow feathers on their heads.

Snorkeling in the morning. Hiking through misty forest by afternoon. E-foiling along the coastline before sunset. The answer is yes.

For @filipe_deandrade, this is life in the Seychelles, a 115-island archipelago off the east coast of Africa. Adventure can take many forms across the islands, from discovering the abundant marine life of Sainte Anne Marine National Park to exploring Mahé’s forested trails and boulder-lined coastline. This photo was featured in our #NatGeoYourShotBugs challenge.

African wild dogs show off their playful side in Mozambique's Niassa National Reserve in this footage filmed by photographer @ottowhitehead. These social carnivores share the vast landscape around the Lugenda River with lions, hippos, and more than 50,000 people. Here, groups including @niassalionproject support efforts to help local communities and carnivores coexist.

Photos by @joelsartore | Meet Amber, a crested mona monkey I photographed while visiting Park Assango in Gabon. You’ll notice that the fur around her face is yellow marked with wide black stripes running from beside her eyes over to her temples and across the center of her forehead. Retiring at 100 years old? Not a chance! Here’s a sneak peek of Sir David Attenborough working on the narration for the upcoming BLUE PLANET III.

#DavidAttenborough100 #DavidAttenborough #BluePlanetIII

Bet you didn’t see that coming 👀
 
Buried beneath the sand, angel sharks can lie perfectly camouflaged and wait for days for prey to swim by. Once a fish gets close enough, they burst from the seabed to strike. But does this technique always work?
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Four billion years of evolution, brought to life on T-shirts. 🧬 🦠

Inspired by the extraordinary stories and iconic animals featured in Evolution, explore the collection and shop with Teemill via the link in our bio.
 
#Evolution #Merch #Design #Tshirt

Finding your feet 👣

Over 500 million years ago, flecks of food drifting on ocean currents were eaten by small animals on the seabed, but the flow would often change. To reach them, some tried a pioneering action: they would move. These are thought to be some of the first animal tracks on Earth.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Who knew the ocean has a public transport system 🦀
 
Columbus crabs aren’t built for long-distance swimming, so this little crab takes a shortcut through the open ocean. By hitchhiking a ride on a turtle, he find transport, a new home and some unexpected company.
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

More than meets the eye 👀

Ancient ancestors of the dolphin hid from the sun’s UV rays using two light-detecting spots. Fascinatingly, some inherited mutations that allowed them to perceive light and shade together, so they could visualise their environment - essentially becoming the first proper eyes.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

From fantasy to reality 🦇

Evolution presenter @chrisgpackham2 reveals how coming face-to-face with some extraordinary bats fulfilled a childhood dream.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Turns out the forest has a group chat 📞
 
Treehoppers might be tiny, but they’ve got plenty to say! They communicate through vibrations sent along the plants they live on, most of which are too quiet for us to hear. But when danger appears, sending the right signal can make all the difference. 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Becoming 'Ant Enemy Number One' 🐜

Army ants are very protective of their colonies, as @chrisgpackham2 found out. Chris reveals how he tackled the challenge of presenting to camera whilst being bitten in some surprisingly painful places! 

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Man’s best friend 🐶

Dogs move differently to humans. They have a digitigrade posture, which means they walk on their toe bones. This anatomy allows longer and more efficient strides so they run faster and jump further. With less surface area touching the ground, they also move with more agility and greater stealth.

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

That’s one lucky impala 
 
Leopards rely on stealth and lightening speed to bring down prey, but a successful hunt can quickly attract unwanted attention. When a spotted hyena arrives to challenge the leopard’s hard-earned catch, an unexpected chain of events unfolds.
